newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt to set up independent Food Safety Board.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt to set up independent Food Safety Board.

text.p: The Irish government on Wednesday approved the establishment of an independent Food Safety Board which will report to the minister for health.

The primary concern of the board will be the protection of public health and it will have full legal powers to ensure that Ireland's various regulatory authorities comply with specific hygiene and safety standards.

"It will ensure that the safety standards that should be applied by various departments and agencies are applied. It will have a policing role and an audit role," health minister Michael Noonan told Irish radio.
Noonan said the board would also have legislative power to bring in outside agencies and consultancies to work for them.
The establishment of the board follows the scare over mad cow disease and growing consumer concern about the presence of antibiotic residues and growth hormones in some Irish meat.
The move was welcomed by the Irish Consumers Association which had called on the government to set up an independent food board to protect the interest of the consumer.
